_comment: NOT IMPLEMENTED: 'Until end of turn, an Aphrodias you control costs {r} less to activate and gets "Whenever this deals damage to an opposing hero, create a Lightning Flow token."' Both halves act on a TARGET PERMANENT for a turn, and neither exists: activation-cost deltas come only from the controller's hero (play._hero_activation_cost_delta) or from the queued 'your next attack with it' one-shots, and Card.granted_abilities -- which dsl.dispatch already fires -- is written in exactly one place, the queued-attack-mod consumption in play.py. The reader exists; the writer does not. Blade Break is printed and handled generically. What was here instead: an INJECT_TRIGGER on ON_ACTIVATE (a trigger this card has no reason to hang on) wrapping a PAY_OR_DAMAGE with amount -1 standing in for the cost reduction -- PAY_OR_DAMAGE is a player CHOICE to pay or take damage, not a cost modifier, so the clause was not merely unimplemented but replaced by an unrelated one. The nested trigger also passed 'opponent': true to ATTACK_TARGET_IS_HERO, which reads no such key, so 'an OPPOSING hero' was any hero. Definition of done: a targeted, duration-scoped ability grant that writes granted_abilities, and a per-object activation-cost delta.
